acceptance: Journey, red first: a floor run fails a test that the diff adds, the retake is green, and the floor fails with a correction that names the test as the cycle's own flaky new test.
A floor run that fails an existing test and retakes green still passes with BUILD_FLOOR_RETAKE_GREEN.
The signal fields name the test and the reason class, so evolve ci classify can read it.
Docs: the core package note and the floor spec change in STE; 100% coverage on each changed function; zero code comments.
fix: When the first floor run fails a top-level test that the cycle's diff adds (the added-test-name source that gateclass already derives from the diff), a green retake does not clear it: the outcome is red, with a reason that names the test as a flaky new test and asks the builder to make it deterministic. A failed test that already exists on the base keeps the retake rule.
summary: Cycle 2353 (2026-11-13): the build floor ran ./cmd/evolve red on TestLaneResume_TwoLanesOfOneScopeAdoptAPausedCycleExactlyOnce twice (14:33Z and 15:14Z). Each time the serialized retake was green, so go/internal/core/build_floor_retake.go retakeFloorOutcome emitted BUILD_FLOOR_RETAKE_GREEN and the build went on. The test is not on main: the cycle added it. At 15:39Z the ship added-test backstop (go/internal/phases/ship/repocontract.go runAddedTestBackstop) ran it once, red, and aborted ship. The cycle then spent an audit, a TDD and a build round (about 1 hour) on the same flaky test. The retake rule exists to forgive an inherited flake, not a new test whose flakiness the cycle introduces and that ship will refuse.
title: A green floor retake does not clear a test that the cycle itself added
